metadata.notes: Expanded clause-level entries and added structured fields for numeric limits to make automated comparisons easier.

concrete_cover.title: Nominal Concrete Cover for Durability
concrete_cover.description: Minimum clear distance from concrete surface to outermost reinforcement bar to protect steel from environmental ingress.
concrete_cover.keywords: concrete cover clear durability corrosion crack width water tank bridge marine exposure

clauses.title: Minimum cover - Mild exposure
clauses.text: Prescriptive nominal minimum cover for mild exposure conditions.

structured.notes: Use 20 mm for reinforced concrete in mild exposure per Table 16.

clauses.title: Minimum cover - Severe exposure
clauses.text: Prescriptive nominal minimum cover for severe exposure conditions.

structured.notes: 45 mm typical for severe exposure in IS 456 Table 16.

clauses.title: Liquid-retaining faces
clauses.text: Minimum cover for liquid-retaining faces is specified as a flat minimum independent of bar size.

structured.notes: IS 3370 requires 45 mm minimum for liquid-retaining faces.

clauses.title: Moderate exposure (in-situ)
clauses.text: Moderate exposure in-situ minimum cover.

clauses.title: Severe exposure (precast)
clauses.text: Severe exposure precast minimum cover.

clauses.title: Extreme exposure (in-situ)
clauses.text: Extreme exposure in-situ minimum cover.

clauses.title: XC1 / S4 minimum
clauses.text: Mapped by structural class and exposure; example: XC1 S4.

structured.notes: Eurocode minimums depend on structural class S1..S6 and exposure; 15 mm appears for XC1/S4 in guidance tables.

clauses.title: XC3 / S6 minimum (example)
clauses.text: XC3 with a high structural class can require larger cover.

structured.notes: Representative mapping: XC2/XC3 S6 -> 30 mm

clauses.title: Cast against earth
clauses.text: When concrete is cast against earth, a larger minimum cover is required.

structured.notes: ACI prescriptive table: 3 in (75 mm) for cast-against-earth.

clauses.title: Exposed to weather
clauses.text: Exposed to weather prescriptive cover values depending on bar size.

structured.notes: Example: 2 in (50 mm) for #6 to #18 bars; smaller bars may use 38 mm.

clauses.title: Probabilistic durability design
clauses.text: Performance-based probabilistic formulation linking target reliability to required cover.

structured.notes: Requires diffusion/carbonation models and target reliability index beta.

shell_buckling.title: Steel Shell Buckling Stability
shell_buckling.description: Buckling checks for thin-walled cylindrical or conical steel shells under axial compression, bending, and shear load conditions.
shell_buckling.keywords: steel buckling shell local buckling shell stability imperfection tower cylinder pipe container knock-down

clauses.title: Diameter-to-thickness classification
clauses.text: Classification limits based on d/t and epsilon factors; semi-compact limits.

structured.notes: Use epsilon = sqrt(235/f_y) typically; classification drives local buckling checks.

clauses.title: Local buckling stress formula
clauses.text: Approximate critical local buckling stress for thin shells.

structured.notes: Analytical expression for thin shell local buckling.

clauses.title: Meridional and hoop buckling interaction
clauses.text: Checks meridional and hoop stresses against buckling boundaries and applies reduction factors per fabrication class.

clauses.title: Fabrication tolerance classes
clauses.text: Applies knock-down factors based on fabrication class (A/B/C) to shell buckling capacity.

clauses.title: D/t limits for HSS
clauses.text: Prescriptive D/t limits and critical stress formula for HSS sections.

clauses.title: Combined loading buckling interaction
clauses.text: Utilization index combining axial, hoop and shear effects via exponent-sum formulation.

structured.notes: Used for large thin-walled shell components.

clauses.title: Geometrically nonlinear analysis with imperfections (GNIA)
clauses.text: Require GNIA with mapped imperfections to assess buckling; links initial imperfection amplitude to manufacturing tolerance.

concrete_breakout.title: Anchor Bolt Concrete Breakout Strength
concrete_breakout.description: Concrete tension breakout capacity of anchors and anchor groups using CCD and related models.
concrete_breakout.keywords: anchor bolt concrete breakout tension foundation base plate embedment attachment anchor group CCD pullout

clauses.title: Isolated anchor tensile capacity (simplified)
clauses.text: Simplified isolated tensile capacity check using concrete tensile strength and projected area.

structured.notes: IS 456 lacks comprehensive CCD group model; use simplified checks for isolated anchors.

clauses.title: Single anchor concrete capacity
clauses.text: ACI CCD single-anchor reference area and nominal resistance formulae.

structured.notes: See Chapter 17 for factors and psi modifiers.

clauses.title: Anchor group breakout capacity
clauses.text: Group capacity computed with area ratios and modification factors.

structured.formula: N_cbg = (A_Nc/A_Nco) * psi_ec_N * psi_ed_N * psi_c_N * psi_cp_N * N_b
structured.notes: Standardized group interaction model.

clauses.title: Group breakout (Eurocode)
clauses.text: Group breakout capacity using reference single-anchor resistance scaled by actual group area and psi factors.

structured.formula: N_Rk,c = N0_Rk,c * (A_c,N / A0_c,N) * psi_s,N * psi_re,N * psi_ec,N * psi_p,N
structured.notes: Consistent unified format across jurisdictions.

clauses.title: Breakout scaling for fatigue
clauses.text: Scale static CCD capacity for high-cycle fatigue and cyclic repetition conditions.

structured.notes: Apply additional reduction factors for cyclic effects as recommended in Bulletin 58.

minimum_reinforcement.title: Minimum Reinforcement (Tension, Compression, Shear)
minimum_reinforcement.description: Prescriptive minimum steel area thresholds for structural concrete elements to prevent brittle failure, control cracking, and ensure minimum ductility.
minimum_reinforcement.keywords: minimum reinforcement area tension compression shear torsion steel ductility crack control As_min rho_min

clauses.title: Minimum flexural reinforcement for beams (tension)
clauses.text: Minimum area of tension steel for beams expressed as As >= 0.85 b d / f_y.

structured.notes: Prevent brittle failure after crack initiation.

clauses.title: Minimum longitudinal reinforcement for columns
clauses.text: Typical recommended percentage range for columns.

structured.notes: Expressed as 0.8% to 6% typically.

clauses.title: Minimum flexural reinforcement for beams
clauses.text: Two candidate formulae; take the greater of the two expressions.

structured.formula: A_s,min = max( (3*sqrt(f'_c)/f_y) * b_w * d , (200/f_y) * b_w * d )
structured.notes: f'_c is cylinder strength in ACI notation.

clauses.title: Minimum reinforcement for columns
clauses.text: Column reinforcement minimums expressed as bounds on A_st / A_g.

structured.notes: Translate to percent as needed (1%..8%).

clauses.title: Minimum flexural reinforcement - Eurocode
clauses.text: A_s,min linked to mean tensile strength of concrete and characteristic yield of steel.

structured.notes: f_ctm is mean tensile strength of concrete.

clauses.title: Minimum longitudinal reinforcement for columns
clauses.text: Column longitudinal minimums driven by axial load demands; see clause for details.

structured.notes: Often expressed as required As based on design axial load and characteristic steel strength.

clauses.title: Minimum reinforcement from crack-control standpoint
clauses.text: Performance-based expression for minimum reinforcement using effective tensile strength and stress distribution coefficients.

structured.notes: Parameters require interpretation; performance-focused.

concrete_properties.title: Concrete Characteristic Strength & Material Definitions
concrete_properties.description: Standardized material strength parameters, specimen definitions (Cube vs Cylinder), and design conversions across major codes.
concrete_properties.keywords: fck fck_cube fck_cyl fctm fcd fctd f_cm conversion cube cylinder phi gamma_m

clauses.title: Specimen standard and grades
clauses.text: 150 mm cube at 28 days used for characteristic strength (f_ck).

clauses.title: Design compressive strength formula
clauses.text: Design compressive strength f_cd from characteristic cube strength and partial factor.

clauses.title: Cylinder vs cube mapping
clauses.text: Eurocode uses cylinder strength as primary; mapping to cube provided in tables.

structured.notes: Users must convert if using cube-based data.

clauses.title: Design compressive strength
clauses.text: Design compressive strength using alpha_cc and gamma_C.

structured.notes: alpha_cc accounts for long term effects and load type.

clauses.title: Cylinder specimen standard
clauses.text: 6x12 inch cylinder used for f'_c at 28 days in ACI practice.

structured.notes: ACI uses f'_c and reduction factors phi for capacity scaling.

clauses.title: Design strength scaling
clauses.text: Uses nominal reduction factors (phi) rather than partial safety factors in some formulations.

structured.notes: Different conceptual approach to partial factors compared to limit state codes.

clauses.title: Mean compressive strength and cube equivalence
clauses.text: Defines mean strength f_cm = f_ck + Delta f and conversion arrays between cube and cylinder.

structured.notes: Provides explicit conversion guidance for analytical comparisons.
